commands.tip: Run after deployments, plugin/theme updates, and database imports. If something looks wrong after an update — this is the first command to try.

commands.tip: If this returns 'Default' when you expect Redis — the drop-in is missing or not connected. Check with wp plugin status redis-cache.
Reads a cached value by key and group. Use when debugging whether a value is being cached correctly.
Arguments: key, value, group, expiration in seconds. Useful for testing cache behavior during debugging.
Removes one cached item by key and group. Use when you need to invalidate a specific value without flushing everything.
Will not overwrite an existing cached value. Useful for testing cache write behavior.

commands.output: Success: 143 transients deleted from the database.
commands.tip: Clears all transients from wp_options. Run alongside wp cache flush for a complete cache clear.
Use --all to delete every transient at once. Useful when debugging stale plugin data.
Use --format=count to see how many transients are stored. A bloated list means wp_options needs cleanup.
Use --format=count to see total count. Use --format=json to pipe into scripts.
Returns the stored value or an error if expired. Use to debug whether a plugin is caching its data correctly.
Third argument is expiration in seconds. 3600 = 1 hour. Use for testing transient behavior in custom plugin code.

commands.output:
Cache commands manage the WordPress object cache and transients.

Available commands:
• wp cache flush                         - Clear entire object cache
• wp cache type                          - Show active cache backend
• wp cache get <key> <group>             - Read a cached value
• wp cache set <key> <value> <group>     - Store a cached value
• wp cache delete <key> <group>          - Remove a cached value
• wp cache add <key> <value> <group>     - Add only if key does not exist
• wp transient delete --all              - Delete all transients
• wp transient list                      - List stored transients
• wp transient get <name>                - Get transient value
• wp transient set <name> <value>        - Set transient with expiry

Cache backends: Default (in-memory), Redis, Memcached

Anchors:
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/cache/#wp-cache-flush
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/cache/#wp-cache-type
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/cache/#wp-transient-get--set--delete
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/cache/#notes-on-cache-backends
commands.tip: wp cache flush + wp transient delete --all = complete cache clear. Run both after migrations and major updates.
